title: Reduction of the actual unbounded integral projection morphism
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $T$ put $R_T=p_T^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}=\varprojlim_{m\geq1}(A/\pi^m)_T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit], and $S_T=(A/\pi^n)_T$, the constant finite quotient ring sheaf, for a fixed $n\geq1$. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D_R(T)=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{R_T})$, $D_S(T)=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{S_T})$ of internal module objects, the derived module pullback and pushforward with their derived adjunction [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and the uncompleted relative derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Set $D_{n,T}K=K\otimes^L_{R_T}S_T$, the derived scalar extension of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

Let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism. Use $L_{f,R}\dashv F_{f,R}$ and $L_{f,S}\dashv F_{f,S}$ and precisely the comparisons $\lambda_f,\rho_{f,n}$ of [lem-sfb-integral-quotient-direct-image-comparison]. Let $\pi^R_{f,K,M}$ and $\pi^S_{f,U,V}$ be the actual module-object projection morphisms, namely the adjuncts of $(\varepsilon_K\otimes1)t_f$, where $t_f:L_f(F_fK\otimes M)\xrightarrow{\sim}L_fF_fK\otimes L_fM$ is the canonical derived pullback-tensor map [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map, def-sfb-module-object-projection-map]. Let
$$b_{T,U,V}:D_{n,T}(U\otimes^L_{R_T}V)\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{n,T}U\otimes^L_{S_T}D_{n,T}V$$
be the canonical derived scalar-tensor balancing map [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], normalized on flat-term K-flat representatives by $(u\otimes v)\otimes s\mapsto(u\otimes1)\otimes(v\otimes s)$.

For every $K\in D_R(X)$ and $M\in D_R(Y)$ the following equality holds in $D_S(Y)$:
$$\begin{aligned}
&\pi^S_{f,D_{n,X}K,D_{n,Y}M}\circ(\rho_{f,n,K}\otimes1)\circ b_{Y,F_{f,R}K,M}\\
&=F_{f,S}\bigl((1\otimes\lambda_{f,M}^{-1})\circ b_{X,K,L_{f,R}M}\bigr)\circ\rho_{f,n,K\otimes L_{f,R}M}\circ D_{n,Y}(\pi^R_{f,K,M}).
\end{aligned}$$
Its source is $D_{n,Y}(F_{f,R}K\otimes^L_{R_Y}M)$ and its target is $F_{f,S}(D_{n,X}K\otimes^L_{S_X}L_{f,S}D_{n,Y}M)$. Thus these specified comparisons identify the reduction of the actual integral projection map with the quotient-coefficient projection map, naturally in both inputs. No properness, completeness, boundedness, constructibility or invertibility of the projection map is assumed.
